changelog: Paraphrased C8 to be shorter and to add an explicit instruction preventing extremely short fragments from being left alone when enforcing cohesion (addresses verb–complement shift side-effect).
Inserted a new Core Principle after C8 prohibiting cuts inside numeric/measurement/time expressions (addresses the primary finding about splitting quantities).
Inserted a new Core Principle after C8 requiring multi-character named entities and transliterations remain contiguous (addresses the finding about splitting names and transliterations).
Replaced C3 with an explicit named-entity rule: forbid cuts inside multi-character names/transliterations so referents remain recoverable (addresses the primary finding).
Replaced C7 with an explicit numeric-expression rule: forbid cuts inside numeral+unit/percentage/duration/speed expressions and treat them as atomic (addresses the measurement-splitting finding).

Paraphrased C2 to be shorter and to add an instruction preventing enforcement of 'no-split' rules from leaving punctuation, quotes, or single-character function words isolated (addresses the verb–complement side-effect).
Replace E1 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_1068 to teach the model about cuts that orphan verbs/punctuation in very short pieces (addresses the primary finding about short-bin harm).
Replace E2 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_974 to show cases where enforcing no verb–complement splits can leave tiny tokens isolated (short latency bin).
Replace E3 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_1025 to expose numeric/measurement and tiny-token isolation tradeoffs in ≤5 bin cases.
Replace E4 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_1413 to give a measured case where splitting numeric/percent spans and adjacent tiny tokens harms cohesion and raises contradiction risk.
Insert a Core Principle forbidding cuts inside numeric/measurement expressions (addresses the primary finding: splitting quantities harms cohesion/contradiction).
Insert a Core Principle requiring multi-character named entities and transliterations remain contiguous (prevents severing referents).

Paraphrase C2 to be shorter and explicitly instruct that enforcing no-split constraints must not leave punctuation, quotes, or single-character function words isolated — attach such tiny tokens to the adjacent phrase (addresses the short-piece harm).
Paraphrase C3 to a shorter form preserving the modifier/head warning (keeps the original judgement but frees space for new rules).
